verses.text: In the twenty-seventh year of Jeroboam king of Israel, Azariah son of Amaziah king of Judah began to reign.
He was sixteen years old when he began to reign, and he reigned fifty-two years in Jerusalem. His mother’s name was Jecoliah of Jerusalem.
He did that which was right in Yahweh’s eyes, according to all that his father Amaziah had done.
However the high places were not taken away. The people still sacrificed and burned incense in the high places.
Yahweh struck the king, so that he was a leper to the day of his death, and lived in a separate house. Jotham, the king’s son was over the household, judging the people of the land.
Now the rest of the acts of Azariah, and all that he did, aren’t they written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Judah?
Azariah slept with his fathers; and they buried him with his fathers in David’s city: and Jotham his son reigned in his place.
In the thirty-eighth year of Azariah king of Judah, Zechariah the son of Jeroboam reigned over Israel in Samaria six months.
He did that which was evil in Yahweh’s sight, as his fathers had done. He didn’t depart from the sins of Jeroboam the son of Nebat, with which he made Israel to sin.
Shallum the son of Jabesh conspired against him, and struck him before the people, and killed him, and reigned in his place.
Now the rest of the acts of Zechariah, behold, they are written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel.
This was Yahweh’s word which he spoke to Jehu, saying, “Your sons to the fourth generation shall sit on the throne of Israel.” So it came to pass.
Shallum the son of Jabesh began to reign in the thirty-ninth year of Uzziah king of Judah, and he reigned for a month in Samaria.
Menahem the son of Gadi went up from Tirzah, came to Samaria, struck Shallum the son of Jabesh in Samaria, killed him, and reigned in his place.
Now the rest of the acts of Shallum, and his conspiracy which he made, behold, they are written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel.

Then Menahem attacked Tiphsah, and all who were in it, and its border areas, from Tirzah. He attacked it because they didn’t open their gates to him, and he ripped up all their women who were with child.
In the thirty ninth year of Azariah king of Judah, Menahem the son of Gadi began to reign over Israel for ten years in Samaria.
He did that which was evil in Yahweh’s sight. He didn’t depart all his days from the sins of Jeroboam the son of Nebat, with which he made Israel to sin.
Pul the king of Assyria came against the land, and Menahem gave Pul one thousand talents  of silver, that his hand might be with him to confirm the kingdom in his hand.

Menahem exacted the money from Israel, even from all the mighty men of wealth, from each man fifty shekels  of silver, to give to the king of Assyria. So the king of Assyria turned back, and didn’t stay there in the land.
Now the rest of the acts of Menahem, and all that he did, aren’t they written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel?
Menahem slept with his fathers, and Pekahiah his son reigned in his place.
In the fiftieth year of Azariah king of Judah, Pekahiah the son of Menahem began to reign over Israel in Samaria for two years.
He did that which was evil in Yahweh’s sight. He didn’t depart from the sins of Jeroboam the son of Nebat, with which he made Israel to sin.

Pekah the son of Remaliah, his captain, conspired against him and attacked him in Samaria, in the fortress of the king’s house, with Argob and Arieh; and with him were fifty men of the Gileadites. He killed him, and reigned in his place.
Now the rest of the acts of Pekahiah, and all that he did, behold, they are written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel.
In the fifty-second year of Azariah king of Judah, Pekah the son of Remaliah began to reign over Israel in Samaria for twenty years.
He did that which was evil in Yahweh’s sight. He didn’t depart from the sins of Jeroboam the son of Nebat, with which he made Israel to sin.

In the days of Pekah king of Israel, Tiglath Pileser king of Assyria came and took Ijon, Abel Beth Maacah, Janoah, Kedesh, Hazor, Gilead, and Galilee, all the land of Naphtali; and he carried them captive to Assyria.
Hoshea the son of Elah made a conspiracy against Pekah the son of Remaliah, attacked him, killed him, and reigned in his place, in the twentieth year of Jotham the son of Uzziah.
Now the rest of the acts of Pekah, and all that he did, behold, they are written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel.
In the second year of Pekah the son of Remaliah king of Israel, Jotham the son of Uzziah king of Judah began to reign.
He was twenty-five years old when he began to reign, and he reigned sixteen years in Jerusalem. His mother’s name was Jerusha the daughter of Zadok.
He did that which was right in Yahweh’s eyes. He did according to all that his father Uzziah had done.
However the high places were not taken away. The people still sacrificed and burned incense in the high places. He built the upper gate of Yahweh’s house.
Now the rest of the acts of Jotham, and all that he did, aren’t they written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Judah?
In those days, Yahweh began to send Rezin the king of Syria and Pekah the son of Remaliah against Judah.
Jotham slept with his fathers, and was buried with his fathers in his father David’s city, and Ahaz his son reigned in his place.

footnotes.content: Azariah becomes king, stepping into a line of succession. New beginnings often come quietly, but they matter—each reign is a chance to turn toward the Lord or away from Him.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Sixteen years old, fifty-two years reigning—a long life, a long reign. His mother Jecoliah is named, a quiet note that mothers shape even kings. Perhaps her faith steadied his younger heart.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: He did what was right, following his father's example. Goodness can flow from one generation to the next when a parent's faith runs deep enough to leave a mark.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Even a righteous king leaves high places standing. Partial obedience is a familiar pattern—we do good in one place while compromise grows roots in another. The Lord sees both.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Leprosy struck him—a mystery and a sorrow. Yet the kingdom didn't fall apart; his son Jotham governed in his place. Sometimes our limitations become a doorway for others to step up and serve.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: His acts are written elsewhere, the chronicler notes. How many lives unfold unrecorded, yet seen by the One who counts even the hairs of our heads.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: He slept with his fathers, buried in David's city. Even a king with leprosy received the dignity of a tomb among his ancestors—grace meeting him in death as it had in life.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Zechariah reigns six months. The kingdom of Israel is coming unraveled, throne after throne toppling. We're watching a nation slowly forget the Lord.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: He did evil like his fathers, holding fast to Jeroboam's sins. Some people inherit wealth or a name; Zechariah inherited unfaithfulness and did nothing to break the chain.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Shallum strikes him down before the people and reigns in his stead. The throne passes not by birth but by violence. When a kingdom forgets God's law, men make their own.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Another king's deeds recorded and filed away. History dutifully notes each reign, each coup, each small ambition—and most of it fades like dust.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The word of Yahweh to Jehu comes to pass: four generations on the throne. Even in chaos, the Lord's word holds firm, precise as a whisper kept.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Shallum reigns one month. Some men seize power only to lose it again, their victory hollow and brief. The throne of Israel has become a thing of sand.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Menahem rises from Tirzah and strikes down Shallum. Coup follows coup; the strong crush the weak. This is what a kingdom looks like when God is forgotten.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Shallum's conspiracy noted in the chronicles. Each small crime, each seized moment, written down—and then ignored. Ambition writes its own epitaph.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Menahem attacks Tiphsah with cruel violence. He rips up pregnant women. This is conquest without mercy, power without conscience—the wages of a nation that has turned its back.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Menahem reigns ten years. He's brutal, and he lasts—which is its own kind of judgment on Israel. Long enough to do much harm.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: He does evil, holding to Jeroboam's sins. Some men inherit a kingdom; Menahem inherits and preserves a legacy of turning away from the Lord.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Pul of Assyria comes, and Menahem pays tribute to hold the throne. The shadow of Assyria lengthens—the great power watching, waiting, ready to swallow the kingdom whole.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Menahem taxes his own people to pay a foreign king. The wealthy are stripped to fund his throne. This is the fruit of unfaithfulness—all the people suffer.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: His acts are written down. A man known for cruelty, taxing his people, buying time with another nation's silver—remembered, but not honored.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Menahem sleeps with his fathers, and Pekahiah takes the throne. One man's long ambition ends, and another's begins. The wheel turns, and the pattern holds.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Pekahiah reigns two years. The throne's pace quickens; the kingdom is spinning apart. Each king's reign grows shorter as the center fails to hold.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: He does evil, never departing from Jeroboam's sins. By now it's not even a choice—it's the air the kingdom breathes. Evil becomes the normal thing.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Pekah, the captain, conspires and strikes Pekahiah down—fifty men with swords in the king's own fortress. The palace itself becomes a tomb. No one is safe.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Pekahiah's reign is recorded and filed away—two years of rule, ended by a captain's ambition and fifty swords. Even a king's brief life is written down.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Pekah reigns twenty years—the longest of these kings. But length of reign isn't peace; it's a measure of how deep evil runs.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: He does evil, walking in Jeroboam's sins—twenty years of it. A long kingdom, forgotten God, and a nation that has lost its way.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Tiglath-Pileser of Assyria comes and carries away Naphtali and Galilee. The exile begins. What a nation builds in unfaithfulness, a foreign king tears down.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Hoshea conspires against Pekah and strikes him down. Another king falls by the sword. Even long reigns end in blood.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Pekah's acts are recorded. The kingdom is shrinking, Assyria is advancing, and the chronicler writes it all down—a long slow fade into exile.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Jotham of Judah begins his reign. While the north is tearing itself apart, the south still has a king—a turn in the story, though trouble is gathering.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: He was twenty-five, reigned sixteen years. Jotham's mother was Jerusha, daughter of Zadok—another mother whose name is kept. Perhaps hers too was a steady faith.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: He did what was right, as his father Uzziah had done. Even in a dark time, faithfulness can run from father to son, holding a small light steady.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: High places remain, yet he builds the upper gate of the Lord's house. Partial faithfulness again—the high places not destroyed, but the Lord's temple still honored.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: His deeds are written in Judah's chronicles. A faithful king, doing right—his story is preserved, set apart from the chaos consuming the north.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: In those days, Yahweh began to send Rezin of Syria and Pekah of Israel against Judah. The storm clouds gathering—and even faithfulness won't hold back the judgment a nation brings on itself.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Jotham sleeps with his fathers, buried with his ancestors. Even the faithful die; Ahaz comes after him. One era ends, and the next—full of trouble—begins.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight
